findings.title: Buttons must have discernible text on states.html
findings.plain: A button has no name, so a screen reader announces it only as "button" and its user cannot tell what it does.
findings.fix: Give it a name: visible text inside the button, or an aria-label that says what it does, such as aria-label="Search".

elements.failure:
Fix any of the following:
  Element does not have inner text that is visible to screen readers
  aria-label attribute does not exist or is empty
  aria-labelledby attribute does not exist, references elements that do not exist or references elements that are empty
  Element has no title attribute
  Element does not have an implicit (wrapped) <label>
  Element does not have an explicit <label>
  Element's default semantics were not overridden with role="none" or role="presentation"

rule.help: Elements must meet minimum color contrast ratio thresholds

findings.title: Elements must meet minimum color contrast ratio thresholds on states.html
findings.plain: Text is too faint against its background for many people to read, people with low vision among them, and anyone looking at a screen in bright light.
findings.fix: Darken the text or lighten its background, or the other way round, until the contrast ratio is at least 4.5 to 1, or 3 to 1 for large text.

elements.html: This note is dark grey on near black in the dark colour scheme.

A focus indicator drawn away from the element (outside it, its two nearest ancestors' styles, and a few pixels around it) is not seen; check focus by hand where a design draws it elsewhere (WCAG 2.4.7).
Whether every image's alternative text says what the image is for (WCAG 1.1.1).
Whether headings and labels describe what follows them (WCAG 2.4.6).
Whether anything is shown by colour alone (WCAG 1.4.1).
Whether everything is still readable and usable at 200% zoom (WCAG 1.4.4).
Whether the page works at 320 px wide without scrolling sideways (WCAG 1.4.10).
